item.claim: The changelog says, with no qualifier, that a result too large to show as a table now produces a text block saying the rows could not be displayed. This would fail for a non-empty data-query result in any path where no table block is emitted and the candidate is never added, for example when the table-payload build raises instead of returning None.
item.source_excerpt:
A result too large to show as a table now produces a text
block saying the rows could not be displayed.

item.claim: The changelog says the Markdown answer 'notes how many rows were left out' whenever the display size limit leaves rows out, including when min(N,500) < N.
item.source_excerpt:
When the display size limit
leaves rows out, the table widget shows "Showing the first N of M rows" above
the search bar and the Markdown answer notes how many rows were left out.

A result whose column headers alone are too large to
show, or whose table could not be built, now produces a text block saying the
rows could not be displayed.
item.claim: The release note says a result whose column headers alone are too large to show always produces a text block saying the rows could not be displayed.
item.verify_against: The header-only oversize branch in src/sqllens/_table_payload.py and its callers in src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py and src/sqllens/tools/_format.py
item.verify_hint: Build a DataFrame whose column names alone exceed the display byte budget; confirm the output contains a text block whose message says the rows could not be displayed.

item.claim: The release note says a result whose table could not be built (for any build failure) produces a text block saying the rows could not be displayed.
item.verify_against: The exception and None-return handling around table construction in src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py, and src/sqllens/_table_payload.py
item.verify_hint: Make the table builder raise or return None; confirm the emitted blocks include a text block with the 'could not be displayed' message. Check which exceptions are caught.

item.claim: AC1 requires the widget cut notice to use normal text colour, a 3px accent-coloured left border, and to wrap on narrow frames. The new widget tests check only the notice text and its position, so these styling requirements must be met by the CSS for the cutnotice class in query_results.html.
item.verify_against: CSS rules for the .cutnotice class in src/sqllens/ui/query_results.html
item.verify_hint: Grep 'cutnotice' in src/sqllens/ui/query_results.html. Confirm a border-left of 3px using the accent variable, a color that is not the grey meta colour, and wrapping.

item.claim: The fake CSV state uses camelCase keys rowCount, truncated and rowCap. The test assumes renderTableBlock fills these keys from the block's snake_case row_count, truncated and row_cap. If the real widget uses different state key names, the CSV tests pass against a state shape the widget never produces.
item.verify_against: State construction inside renderTableBlock in src/sqllens/ui/query_results.html
item.verify_hint: Find where renderTableBlock builds the per-block state (grep 'rowCap' and 'rowCount'). Confirm CSV export reads state.rowCap and state.truncated.

item.claim: The CSV warning tests set C to filteredRows().length. AC10 defines C as the number of data rows in the exported file. These are the same only if buildCsvExport writes exactly the filtered (sorted) rows and computes C from that same array.
item.verify_hint: Check that the row count in the warning comes from the same rows array serialized into the CSV body.

item.claim: The test docstring says the prompt must never describe a result table as full. The test checks only five lowercase substrings, so wordings such as 'all of the rows', 'entire table' or 'every row' are not caught.
item.verify_hint: Search default.py for 'entire', 'all rows', 'all of the', 'every row', 'whole table' and 'complete' near result or table wording.

item.claim: AC14 requires the cut-statement rule to cover the agent's final reply when no emit_text call succeeded, and to cover an introduction written before the query runs. The prompt test does not assert either clause, so default.py must contain them.
item.verify_hint: Read the rule near 'states how many rows the table shows' in default.py. Confirm it names the final reply when no emit_text succeeded, and forbids calling the result full or complete in an introduction.
